name: Magical Permutation
description: Kuro has just learned about permutations and he is really excited to create a new permutation type. He has chosen $$$n$$$ distinct positive integers and put all of them in a set $$$S$$$. Now he defines a magical permutation to be: A permutation of integers from $$$0$$$ to $$$2^x - 1$$$, where $$$x$$$ is a non-negative integer. The bitwise xor of any two consecutive elements in the permutation is an element in $$$S$$$. Since Kuro is really excited about magical permutations, he wants to create the longest magical permutation possible. In other words, he wants to find the largest non-negative integer $$$x$$$ such that there is a magical permutation of integers from $$$0$$$ to $$$2^x - 1$$$. Since he is a newbie in the subject, he wants you to help him find this value of $$$x$$$ and also the magical permutation for that $$$x$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains the integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \leq n \leq 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of elements in the set $$$S$$$. The next line contains $$$n$$$ distinct integers $$$S_1, S_2, \ldots, S_n$$$ ($$$1 \leq S_i \leq 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the elements in the set $$$S$$$.
output_specification: In the first line print the largest non-negative integer $$$x$$$, such that there is a magical permutation of integers from $$$0$$$ to $$$2^x - 1$$$. Then print $$$2^x$$$ integers describing a magical permutation of integers from $$$0$$$ to $$$2^x - 1$$$. If there are multiple such magical permutations, print any of them.
approach_summary: Maintain prefix sums and dynamic point updates via Fenwick tree using lowbit operations (i & -i) in O(log N) time and O(N) space.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1163E — Magical Permutation [70. BIT / Fenwick Tree]
topic_editorial.summary: Point updates and range prefix queries with Fenwick Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Every integer $i$ has a unique binary decomposition. Index $i$ in a Binary Indexed Tree stores the cumulative sum of the interval $(i - \text{lowbit}(i), i]$, allowing logarithmic traversal via $i \mathrel{+}= (i \mathbin{\&} -i)$ and $i \mathrel{-}= (i \mathbin{\&} -i)$.
